name: Vercel

fields.name: teamId
fields.label: Team ID (optional, needed for team resources with a Full Account token)

auth.keyHelp: Pick the narrowest scope (one team or one project) and set an expiration; Vercel tokens have no read-only option.

read.label: Get a deployment by ID or URL

tested: mock; real service refused a fake key
notes: No read-only token: the only limit Vercel documents is scope (Full Account, one team, or one project), not permission level. A project-scoped token is the safest option but the KB guide says it is denied team-level and user-level resources, so GET /v2/user (the test call) and list_teams may be refused for a project-scoped token; in that case use /v10/projects as the test. That refusal behaviour is inferred from the guide's wording and was not tested. Full Account tokens need ?teamId= (or &slug=) to reach team resources; team and project tokens do not. Personal access tokens begin vcp_ per the KB guide. Tokens are created from the personal account settings page, even when scoped to a team. No API version header is used; versions are in the path (v10 projects, v7 deployments, v13 deployment by id, v5 domains, v2 user and teams), as listed on the REST API index today. The /v2/user example response nests the account under a user object with username, email, id and name. Official MCP server https://mcp.vercel.com is OAuth only and only works with Vercel-approved MCP clients per the docs. Listing a project's environment values is left out on purpose: those values would reach the assistant.
